newsitem.title: HUNGARY: EXPAND EAST, EX-CEN. BANKER TELLS HUNGARIAN BANKS.
newsitem.headline: EXPAND EAST, EX-CEN. BANKER TELLS HUNGARIAN BANKS.

text.p: Hungary's commercial banks should expand into other east European countries, offering their superior experience with financial markets, the former vice president of the central bank said on Friday.

"Hungary's financial sector is the most developed in the region and our banks have the opportunity to export some of this expertise." Sandor Czirjak, who left the National Bank of Hungary late last year, told a professional conference.

Hungary was the first in East Europe to set up a stock market in 1990 and is the only country with a western-style commodities market. It also has interbank money and currency markets and several years of experience with financial derivatives.
Several Hungarian banks have set up branches in the Balkans and the former Soviet Union over the last few years.
